title: Cross-region model handovers: compatibility heuristics and operational notes
content:
Purpose
This note collects pragmatic heuristics and an operational compatibility scoring approach for cross-region model handovers. Goal is to reduce unexpected behavior when the control plane routes requests across regions or falls back to compatible model variants during outages or capacity skews.

Scope and motivating examples
- Multi-region serving: user requests originating in eu-west may be served from us-central as a fallback.
- Gradual rollouts: a canary version in us-west should not break eu customers if routed there.
- Capacity mismatch: dedicated pools in region A are saturated and requests route to region B where a different quantized build/version exists.

Why this matters
- Small differences (tokenization, padding, response shape, function-calling signatures) can surface as prod incidents.
- Consumers rely on stable semantics (embedding dimensionality, deterministic function-call keys).

High-level constraints
- Backwards-compatibility preference: prefer models that preserve public API contract (response schema, embedding dims).
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: prefer local region variants unless score delta exceeds threshold.
- Security/isolation: private deployments must not route outside an allowed region boundary unless explicit opt-in.

Compatibility attributes (canonical set to evaluate)
1) API contract: function call schemas, structured output shapes, streaming behavior (yes/no)
2) Tokenization: tokenizer family + vocabulary hash
3) Embedding spec: dimension, normalization, dtype
4) Model family and major semver: architecture family (e.g., transformer-x) + major version
5) Quantization & kernels: q4_0 vs q8_0 and required runtime kernels/backends
6) Latency profile: p50/p95 on representative request type
7) Determinism: seed & sampling default behavior (e.g., temperature handling)
8) Security constraints: private-only flags, KMS-bound models

Simple scoring heuristic (operationally lightweight)
- Each attribute gets a weight (sums to 100): API contract 30, Tokenizer 20, Embedding 15, Model family 10, Quantization/kernels 10, Latency 10, Security 5.
- Attribute match categories: exact match = 0 penalty, compatible = small penalty, incompatible = large penalty.
- Total penalty -> compatibility score = 100 - penalty. Thresholds: >=85 = safe; 65–84 = caution (requires routing policy override); <65 = block.

Example scoring table (toy)
Attributes: API/Token/Embed/Family/Quant/Latency/Sec
Candidate A (region-local): exact/exact/exact/exact/exact/ok/exact -> penalty 0 -> score 100
Candidate B (other-region quantized): exact/compatible/compatible/compatible/incompatible/slow/exact -> penalty 40 -> score 60 -> block
Candidate C (other-region same model family): compatible/exact/exact/compatible/compatible/slower/blocked: penalty 20 -> score 80 -> caution

Operational routing rules (priority list)
1) Enforce security boundaries: if model has private-only or region-isolation flag, do not route outside allowed boundary.
2) Prefer local region candidate with score >=75.
3) If local region lacks a candidate >=75, evaluate cross-region candidates by score and latency delta. Add soft penalty for >=100ms RTT.
4) For live rollouts: if rolling a new major model, only route if candidate score >=90 for regions marked as production. For non-prod regions allow 80.
5) Canary fallback: allow requests to be handled by canary variant only for deterministic workloads and if compatibility score >=92.
6) Auto-fallback degrade path: when a candidate is chosen with score between 75–84, tag responses with header X-Model-Compat: caution and increment telemetry counter.

Control plane metadata recommendations
- Registry entries should include explicit normalized attributes for the scoring engine: tokenizer_hash, embedding_dim, api_schema_sha256, quant_profile, latency_profile_key, privacy_tags.
- Store computed compatibility fingerprints so cross-region checks are O(1) at routing time.
- Version aliases: maintain mapping alias -> version list + stability label (stable/beta/canary).

Telemetry and alerting
- Emit compatibility.score and compatibility.reasons (list of short codes) whenever a non-local candidate is selected.
- Alert when >1% of requests in a region are handled by candidates with score <80 for >10m.
- Record user-visible regressions (e.g., embedding dim mismatch) as high-severity incidents.

Runbook snippets
- On region capacity pressure: check top-3 candidate scores for the affected model across regions and verify none are blocked. If blocked, trigger emergency worker to spin up compatible model in-region or scale dedicated pool.
- On rollout rollback: if telemetry shows caution flags spiking, immediately pin region routes to previous stable alias and start a postmortem.

Examples of edge cases and mitigations
- Tokenizer mismatch where embedding dims equal: treat tokenizer mismatch as high penalty for generated-text APIs, but lower penalty for embedding-only routes.
- Function-calling schema drift: block routing unless schema is a strict superset with backward compatibility markers.
- Quantization kernel missing in target region: add an automatic compatibility hint to suggest a fallback quantization plan or queue a model build job.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Fine-tune attribute weights: should API contract be 40%? business ask vs infra impact tradeoff.
- How to version and sign api_schema consistently across internal toolchains.
- Mechanism for customers to opt-in to relaxed compatibility for latency-first fallbacks.

Next steps (short list)
- Build a small scoring prototype as a lambda service and run A/B on two test models for eu/us routing in staging. (Owner: Diego)
- Add metadata fields to registry schema: tokenizer_hash + api_schema_sha256 (Owner: Priya)
- Draft control-plane routing policy PR with the priority list above for review (Owner: Aisha)

References and links
- Confluence: Model Registry Overview (linked above)
- RFC: rollout-aliases-and-stability (internal RFC id: RFC-2024-09-model-rollout)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: prefer simple binary/threshold checks initially rather than a heavy ML-based compatibility predictor. We can evolve once we have stable telemetry.
- Look for missing attributes we might need for domain-specific models (e.g., vision patch size, lat-long for geofenced models).

---
Quick scratchpad (examples to test in prototype)
- Build two registry entries: base-model-v1 (eu build q8), base-model-v1-us (us build q4) -> expected score ~72 due to quant/kernel mismatch but API same.
- Test routing with embedding-only requests vs chat generation requests and compare caution counters.
